key_idea: A strictly ascending deal picks K distinct values and one card of each, so the answer is the K-th elementary symmetric polynomial of the ten counts.
sketch: Compute e_k(n_1..n_10) with the standard knapsack-style recurrence e[j] += e[j-1]*n_i iterating j downward, O(10*K). The order of the deal is forced by the ascending condition, so no extra factorial is needed. Pitfall: the result can reach 100^10 = 1e20, which overflows unsigned 64-bit (1.8e19), so use unsigned __int128 (or big integers) and print it digit by digit; also handle the zero answer when printing manually.
